correctness.rationale: Derived the Cauchy–Binet determinant as a sum of strictly positively weighted squared sines of pairwise node-angle differences. For 2/3 Gauss nodes the common direction occurs at the displayed exact integer multiples of pi sqrt(3) and 10pi/sqrt(15), respectively. Four-node singularity would force rational a/b from both symmetric node pairs, whereas (a/b)^2=(23+4 sqrt(30))/7 is irrational. Continued fractions give infinitely many q with |q a/b-p|<1/q, and testing perpendicular direction yields the pi^2/q^2 eigenvalue upper bound. Undamped exact W/h has eigenvalues 1/2 ± |sin(omega h)|/(2|omega|h), so the operator-norm discrepancy tends to 1/2. Independent numeric weighted determinants and convergents corroborate the derivation but are not its proof.
residual_risks: Applies to direct quadrature of the integral for a planar rotational pair only, not to Gauss Runge–Kutta update maps or general matrices. Numerical near-resonance checks do not certify arbitrarily large steps.

value.rationale: Positive definite rather than merely positive semidefinite quadrature is a natural rank-preservation design question. The sharp four-node threshold and infinite badly conditioned subsequence show rigorously that unconditional algebraic rank retention need not imply robust approximation, a structural warning for direct Gramian quadrature.
residual_risks: All-step guarantee is specific to a two-dimensional rank-one rotating system; not a theorem for generic high-dimensional Gramians.

final_claim: For rank-one forced planar rotations with damping gamma>=0 and nonzero angular frequency, direct s-node Gauss–Legendre Gramian quadratures are singular infinitely often at s=1,2,3, and s=4 is strictly positive for every step h>0; undamped G4/h has inverse-square almost-resonant eigenvalues while W/h tends to I/2.
limitations: Applies to direct quadrature of the integral for a planar rotational pair only, not to Gauss Runge–Kutta update maps or general matrices. Numerical near-resonance checks do not certify arbitrarily large steps.
